narrative.overview: The site reads as a small printed field guide to services. Each app is a numbered plate identified by field marks (stack, status, updated) rather than a screenshot card. A spruce book-cloth rail holds the name and contents; the reading column is cool plate paper with near-black ink.
keyCharacteristics: Spruce cloth rail on the left, paper column beside it; dark theme keeps the cloth.
One vermilion pointer for focus, hover, current-page arrow, field-mark labels and the single primary action.
Square corners, 1px borders, no shadows, no side-stripe borders.
Serif for reading and headings, mono for labels, field marks, controls and code.
Status is always a glyph plus a word.

rules.name: The One Pointer Rule
rules.body: Vermilion is the only accent and never fills a surface larger than a button. Its rarity is how the eye finds the next action.

rules.name: The Cloth Stays Rule
rules.body: The rail is spruce in both themes; only the paper changes.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Serif reads, mono indexes. Never set a paragraph in mono or a heading in anything but Spectral 800.

rules.name: The Flat Print Rule
rules.body: Nothing casts a shadow. Separate with a border or a tone shift.

dos: Do keep vermilion to pointers, field-mark labels, focus and the single primary action.
Do pair every status with its glyph and word.
Do use plain labels: Project, Stack, Status, Updated, Fig. 1.
Do separate surfaces with 1px borders and keep corners square.
Do keep targets at least 2.75rem and honor reduced motion.
Do render unknown facts as a visible TODO box, never as invented copy.
donts: Don't add shadows, gradients, glass, rounded corners or side-stripe borders.
Don't use "Plate" or "Field marks" as visible words; the user chose plain labels.
Don't set body copy in mono or headings in anything but Spectral 800.
Don't put vermilion on large fills or use it for decoration.
Don't build SaaS-landing hero patterns or stock illustration.
